implementation_constraints: pure stdlib only, no third-party imports
reads entire stdin, writes single-line JSON result to stdout, exits 0 on both success and validation-error paths
never raises/exits non-zero — all error conditions funnel to printing the literal string ERROR

unresolved_intent.decision: reject bool values for priority (True/False) even though Python's bool is an int subclass
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec says priority: int; silently accepting True/False as 1/0 would be surprising and not clearly intended by the contract, so it is treated as malformed input -> ERROR

unresolved_intent.ir_region: job object with unexpected extra keys
unresolved_intent.decision: ignore any keys beyond id/priority/needs/fails rather than rejecting the job
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec's job shape lists these fields but does not say extra keys are forbidden; being lenient here avoids over-rejecting otherwise well-formed input

unresolved_intent.decision: treat an explicit "needs": null the same as an absent needs field (empty list)
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec says needs absent = none; null is the closest JSON equivalent to absence and treating it as a hard error felt overly strict for an otherwise well-formed job

unresolved_intent.ir_region: scheduling loop termination when no job is READY but undecided jobs remain
unresolved_intent.decision: break the loop defensively rather than raising an error, since upfront cycle/unknown-need validation guarantees this branch is unreachable
unresolved_intent.rationale: keeps the runtime scheduler simple and total for valid input; the defensive break is dead code reachable only if validation has a gap, and is safer than an infinite loop
